tldr: This paper introduces BTGenBot, a system that fine-tunes lightweight LLMs (up to 7B parameters) on a dataset of 600 behavior trees to generate robot-executable behavior trees from natural language descriptions, demonstrating that compact models can achieve comparable effectiveness to larger counterparts.
contributions: A dataset of 600 behavior trees paired with GPT-3.5-generated natural language task descriptions, sourced from open-source robotics projects
A comprehensive evaluation system testing generated behavior trees across nine tasks using static syntactical analysis, a custom validator, simulated environment (TurtleBot3), and a real robot
A comparative analysis of three LLMs (Llama-2-7b, Llama-2-7b-chat, CodeLlama-7b-Instruct) and their fine-tuned versions
methods: The authors created an instruction-following dataset by collecting 600 behavior trees from open-source robotics projects and using GPT-3.5 to generate corresponding natural language descriptions. Three 7B-parameter models were fine-tuned using a two-step process: first with the Alpaca dataset for instruction-following, then with the custom behavior tree dataset using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with expanded target modules including MLP layers. Evaluation was conducted in two phases: Phase 1 assessed simpler tasks (1-7) using inference time, syntactic correctness (via Groot2), and semantic evaluation by human experts; Phase 2 tested all nine tasks using a custom BT validator, simulation, and real robot deployment.
results: In Phase 1 syntactic evaluation, fine-tuned models achieved 86-86-86% (zero-shot) and 86-86-86% (one-shot) correctness for Alpaca, LlamaChat, and CodeLlama respectively. Fine-tuned CodeLlama reached 100% syntactic correctness in zero-shot. Semantic evaluation showed fine-tuned CodeLlama achieving 100% in zero-shot but dropping to 57% in one-shot. Base models performed poorly without fine-tuning, with zero-shot base models at 0-0-28% syntactic correctness. All material including dataset, prompts, and validator code is available at https://github.com/AIRLab-POLIMI/BTGenBot.
limitations: The dataset is limited to fewer than 1,000 samples, requiring increased epochs for satisfactory results
Inference time ranges from seconds to minutes depending on task complexity, and some models (Alpaca) fail to terminate generation in certain cases
Natural language descriptions were generated by GPT-3.5, potentially introducing bias
Phase 2 results appear to be incomplete/truncated in the provided text
